records.source: לְדָוִ֨דרִיבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־יְרִיבַ֑י לְ֝חַ֗ם אֶת־לֹֽחֲמָֽי׃
records.gloss: Of David. Contend, YHWH, with my opponents; fight those fighting me.
pieces: Of David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, oppose those who oppose me; do battle with those who battle against me.

L.1: Of David. Contend, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, with those who contend with me; fight against those who fight against me.

R.1: By David. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, take my side against the people who are attacking me. Fight against those who are fighting me.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 32:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: contend: take up a case against
decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is used of a dispute in court (Isaiah 3:13). The psalm moves between two pictures, the law court (verses 11, 23-24) and the battlefield (verses 2-3).

decisions.choice: fight those who fight me: the same words turned back
decisions.reason: Each line repeats one word: let the LORD do to them what they are doing to me.

records.heading: Fight for me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: הַחֲזֵ֣ק מָגֵ֣ן וְצִנָּ֑ה וְ֝ק֗וּמָה בְּעֶזְרָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Take hold of shield and body-shield, and rise up for my help.
pieces: Seize the small shield and the large one, and stand up to help me.

L.2: Take hold of shield and buckler, and rise up as my help.

R.2: Pick up {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} shields like a warrior, and come to help me.

decisions.choice: shield and buckler: a small and a large shield
decisions.reason: The magen was a small round shield; the tsinnah a large shield covering the whole body. Together they mean full armor.

decisions.choice: the LORD as a warrior
decisions.reason: The psalmist pictures the LORD arming for battle on his behalf, as "the LORD is a warrior" (Exodus 15:3; Isaiah 42:13).

decisions.choice: your ... like a warrior
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture explicit (m2).

records.source: וְהָ֘רֵ֤ק חֲנִ֣ית וּ֭סְגֹר לִקְרַ֣את רֹדְפָ֑י אֱמֹ֥ר לְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י יְֽשֻׁעָתֵ֥ךְ אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And draw out spear and lance to meet those pursuing me; say to my soul, your salvation [am] I.
pieces: Draw the spear and battle-axe to face those who chase me; let me hear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, "I am your salvation."

L.3: And draw out spear and battle-axe to meet those who pursue me; say to my soul, "I [am] your salvation."

R.3: Get out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} spear and battle-axe against the people who are chasing me. Tell me, "I am the one who brings you salvation."

decisions.choice: battle-axe: a weapon
alternatives: and close the way (as a verb)
decisions.reason: The word (segor) may be a verb, "close (the way)", or the name of a weapon, probably a kind of axe. Beside "spear" it is taken as a weapon.

decisions.choice: your salvation: the one who saves you
decisions.reason: Salvation (yeshu'ah) is rescue from danger. He asks to hear the LORD himself say that he will save him.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) is the speaker himself.

records.source: יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ וְיִכָּלְמוּ֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֪י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָח֣וֹר וְיַחְפְּר֑וּ חֹ֝שְׁבֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Let them be ashamed and humiliated, those seeking my soul; let them be turned back and abashed, those planning my harm.
pieces: Let those who are hunting for my life be shamed and disgraced; let those who are plotting to hurt me be driven back in confusion.

L.4: Let them be ashamed and disgraced who seek my soul; let them be turned back and confounded who plan my harm.

R.4: The people who want to kill me, let them be ashamed and disgraced. Let the people who plan to hurt me turn back in confusion.

decisions.choice: Let them be ashamed: a prayer against the enemy
decisions.reason: Verses 4-8 and 26 ask God to bring the enemies' plans back on them. Such prayers hand vengeance over to God (Deuteronomy 32:35) rather than taking it, and the psalmist says he had done these people only good (verses 12-14).

decisions.choice: seek my soul: try to kill me
decisions.reason: To seek someone's life (nefesh) is to plan their death (Jeremiah 11:21).

records.source: יִֽהְי֗וּ כְּמֹ֥ץ לִפְנֵי־ר֑וּחַ וּמַלְאַ֖ךְ יְהוָ֣ה דּוֹחֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Let them be like chaff before [the] wind, and the angel of YHWH driving [them].
pieces: May they be like chaff the wind blows off, with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s angel driving them along.

L.5: Let them be like chaff before [the] wind, and the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} driving [them] on.

R.5: Let them be like straw blown away by the wind, with the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chasing them.

decisions.choice: chaff: as in Psalm 1
decisions.reason: Chaff is the light husk that the wind blows away at threshing, the picture of the wicked in 1:4.

decisions.choice: the angel of the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 34:8, where he guards those who fear the LORD; here he drives their enemies away.

records.source: יְֽהִי־דַרְכָּ֗ם חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וַחֲלַקְלַקּ֑וֹת וּמַלְאַ֥ךְ יְ֝הוָ֗ה רֹדְפָֽם׃
records.gloss: Let their way be darkness and slippery places, and the angel of YHWH pursuing them.
pieces: May their path turn dark and slick, with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s angel hunting them down.

L.6: Let their way be darkness and slippery places, and the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pursuing them.

R.6: Let their road be dark and slippery as the angel of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} runs after them.

decisions.choice: a dark, slippery way: no safe footing
decisions.reason: Running in the dark on slippery ground, they cannot escape (Jeremiah 23:12).

decisions.choice: pursuing them: turning the pursuers into the pursued
decisions.reason: They pursue the psalmist (verse 3); now the angel pursues them.

records.source: כִּֽי־חִנָּ֣ם טָֽמְנוּ־לִ֭י שַׁ֣חַת רִשְׁתָּ֑ם חִ֝נָּ֗ם חָפְר֥וּ לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: For without cause they hid for me [the] pit of their net; without cause they dug for my soul.
pieces: For no reason they set a hidden net in a pit for me; for no reason they dug a hole to trap me.

L.7: For without cause they have hidden for me the pit of their net; without cause they have dug [it] for my soul.

R.7: For no reason at all, they hid a net in a pit to trap me. For no reason they dug a hole to catch me.

decisions.choice: a pit and a net: a hunter's trap
decisions.reason: Hunters dug pits and covered them, or hid nets, to catch animals; enemies' schemes are often pictured this way (9:16; 57:7).

decisions.choice: the pit of their net; they dug
alternatives: they hid their net; they dug a pit
decisions.reason: The word "pit" stands in the first line but seems to belong with "dug" in the second. Many read the lines as "they hid their net for me; they dug a pit for my life". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: without cause: for nothing
decisions.reason: The word (chinnam) means freely, for no reason; it returns in verse 19.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: תְּבוֹאֵ֣הוּ שׁוֹאָה֮ לֹֽא־יֵ֫דָ֥ע וְרִשְׁתּ֣וֹ אֲשֶׁר־טָמַ֣ן תִּלְכְּד֑וֹ בְּ֝שׁוֹאָ֗ה יִפָּל־בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Let ruin come [on] him [that] he does not know, and his net which he hid, let it catch him; in ruin let him fall into it.
pieces: Let disaster fall on them before they know it; let the net they hid catch them, and let them drop into it to their ruin.

L.8: Let ruin come on him [that] he does not know, and his net that he hid, let it catch him; into ruin let him fall.

R.8: Let disaster surprise them. Let them get caught in their own net. Let them fall into their own trap and be ruined.

decisions.choice: his own net catches him: evil turns back on its maker
decisions.reason: The trap set for the innocent catches the one who set it (7:16; 9:16).

decisions.choice: him: each of the enemies
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular, speaking of the enemy as one person or of each of them.

decisions.choice: them, they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the enemy as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all of them (m2). Balanced and Readable keep the plural of verses 4-7; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

records.source: וְ֭נַפְשִׁי תָּגִ֣יל בַּיהוָ֑ה תָּ֝שִׂישׂ בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And my soul will rejoice in YHWH; it will exult in his salvation.
pieces: Then my whole being will be glad in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and celebrate the salvation {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings.

L.9: And my soul will rejoice in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it will exult in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation.

R.9: Then I will be happy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will celebrate because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought me salvation.

decisions.choice: And: then, when God has acted
decisions.reason: The joy follows the rescue he has prayed for.

decisions.choice: his salvation: his rescue
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: my whole being (B); I (R)
decisions.reason: "My soul" (nefesh) is the whole self.

records.source: כָּ֥ל עַצְמוֹתַ֨י׀תֹּאמַרְנָה֮ יְהוָ֗ה מִ֥י כָ֫מ֥וֹךָ מַצִּ֣יל עָ֭נִי מֵחָזָ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָנִ֥י וְ֝אֶבְי֗וֹן מִגֹּזְלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: All my bones will say, YHWH, who [is] like you, delivering [the] poor from [one] stronger than he, and [the] poor and needy from [one] robbing him?
pieces: Every bone in my body will say, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, is there anyone like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? You save the helpless from people stronger than they are, the helpless and the poor from those who rob them."

L.10: All my bones will say, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, who [is] like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, delivering [the] poor from [one] too strong for {{gender:them|him}}, and [the] poor and needy from [one] who robs {{gender:them|him}}?"

R.10: With my whole body I will say, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, no one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! You save weak people from those who are too strong for them. You save poor, needy people from those who rob them."

decisions.choice: all my bones: my whole self
decisions.reason: As in 32:3.

decisions.choice: who is like you?: no one compares with the LORD
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one" (Exodus 15:11; Micah 7:18).

decisions.choice: the poor and needy: the helpless
decisions.reason: The two words ('ani, 'evyon) describe people with no power or means to defend themselves.

decisions.choice: them, with "him" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Him" is any poor person. Balanced and Readable use the plural.

records.source: יְ֭קוּמוּן עֵדֵ֣י חָמָ֑ס אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי יִשְׁאָלֽוּנִי׃
records.gloss: Witnesses of violence rise up; [about] what I do not know they ask me.
pieces: Violent witnesses stand up against me and question me about things I know nothing of.

L.11: Witnesses of violence rise up; [of things] that I do not know they question me.

R.11: People stand up in court and tell lies about me. They accuse me of crimes I know nothing about.

decisions.choice: witnesses rise up: in court
decisions.reason: Witnesses stood up to give evidence (Deuteronomy 19:15-16). These are "witnesses of violence" (Exodus 23:1), whose false evidence aims to destroy.

decisions.choice: what I do not know: charges he knows nothing about
decisions.reason: He is questioned about wrongs he never did.

decisions.choice: tell lies about me
decisions.reason: Readable says what these witnesses do (m1).

records.source: יְשַׁלְּמ֣וּנִי רָ֭עָה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָ֗ה שְׁכ֣וֹל לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: They repay me evil in place of good; bereavement [is] to my soul.
pieces: They pay me back harm for good; I am left desolate, like someone who has lost a child.

L.12: They repay me evil in place of good; bereavement [is] to my soul.

R.12: I was good to them, but they pay me back with evil. I feel as lonely as parents whose children have died.

decisions.choice: bereavement: the loss of children
alternatives: lying in wait (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The word (shekol) is the grief of parents who have lost their children (Isaiah 47:8-9). He is left utterly alone.

decisions.choice: evil for good: the worst of wrongs
decisions.reason: To repay good with evil is condemned in Proverbs 17:13; verses 13-14 tell the good he had done them.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֤י׀בַּחֲלוֹתָ֡ם לְב֬וּשִׁי שָׂ֗ק עִנֵּ֣יתִי בַצּ֣וֹם נַפְשִׁ֑י וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י עַל־חֵיקִ֥י תָשֽׁוּב׃
records.gloss: But I, when they were sick, my clothing [was] sackcloth; I humbled with fasting my soul, and my prayer on my bosom returned.
pieces: But as for me, when they lay sick, I dressed in sackcloth; I humbled myself by fasting, and I prayed with my head bent low.

L.13: But I, when they were sick, my clothing [was] sackcloth; I humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned to my bosom.

R.13: But when they were sick, I wore clothes of mourning and went without food. I bowed my head and prayed for them.

decisions.choice: sackcloth: rough clothing of grief
decisions.reason: Sackcloth, made of coarse goat's hair, was worn in mourning and in prayer (2 Samuel 3:31; Genesis 37:34).

decisions.choice: I humbled my soul with fasting
decisions.reason: To humble oneself (literally "afflict the soul") is to go without food and comfort before God (Leviticus 16:29).

decisions.choice: my prayer returned to my bosom: I prayed with head bowed
alternatives: my prayer came back to me unanswered
may my prayer return to me
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure. It may picture him praying bent over with his head on his chest, or say that his prayer for them came back to him unanswered, or wish that the good he prayed for them would come back on himself.

decisions.choice: for them
decisions.reason: Readable says whom he prayed for (verse 13 begins with their sickness).

records.source: כְּרֵֽעַ־כְּאָ֣ח לִ֭י הִתְהַלָּ֑כְתִּי כַּאֲבֶל־אֵ֝֗ם קֹדֵ֥ר שַׁחֽוֹתִי׃
records.gloss: As a friend, as a brother to me, I went about; as one mourning a mother, dark [in mourning] I bowed down.
pieces: I went about as if for a friend or a brother; I bent low, dressed in dark mourning clothes, like one grieving for a mother.

L.14: As [for] a friend, as [for] a brother to me, I went about; like one who mourns a mother, in dark [clothes] I bowed down.

R.14: I acted as if they were my friends or my brothers. I was as sad as someone whose mother has died. I wore dark clothes and bowed my head.

decisions.choice: dark: in the dark clothes of mourning
decisions.reason: The word (qoder) means dark or dirty, the unwashed look and dark clothing of mourners (38:7; 42:10).

decisions.choice: one mourning a mother: the deepest grief
decisions.reason: He grieved for them as for his closest family.

records.source: וּבְצַלְעִי֮ שָׂמְח֪וּ וְֽנֶאֱ֫סָ֥פוּ נֶאֶסְפ֬וּ עָלַ֣י נֵ֭כִים וְלֹ֣א יָדַ֑עְתִּי קָֽרְע֥וּ וְלֹא־דָֽמּוּ׃
records.gloss: But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered; they gathered against me, smiters, and I did not know; they tore and were not silent.
pieces: But when I stumbled, they were glad and gathered together; attackers gathered against me without my knowing it; they ripped into me and would not be quiet.

L.15: But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered; they gathered against me, smiters, and I did not know; they tore [at me] and did not stop.

R.15: But when I had trouble, they were happy. They got together against me. People who attack others came after me, and I did not even know them. They would not stop attacking me.

decisions.choice: smiters: attackers
decisions.reason: The word (nekim) is obscure. It may mean those who strike, or people who are themselves crippled or despised; some read "strangers".

decisions.choice: I did not know: without my knowing, or people I did not know
decisions.reason: The words can mean that they gathered behind his back, or that the attackers were people he did not know.

decisions.choice: tore: tore at me
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear; here probably with words, tearing him to pieces.

decisions.choice: I did not even know them
decisions.reason: Readable follows the second reading in m2.

records.source: בְּ֭חַנְפֵי לַעֲגֵ֣י מָע֑וֹג חָרֹ֖ק עָלַ֣י שִׁנֵּֽימוֹ׃
records.gloss: With godless mockers of [a] cake, gnashing at me their teeth.
pieces: Like ungodly jesters who mock for a bite of food, they ground their teeth at me.

L.16: Like godless mockers for [a] cake, [they] gnashed their teeth at me.

R.16: Like godless people who make fun of others to earn a meal, they ground their teeth at me in hate.

decisions.choice: godless mockers of a cake
alternatives: they mocked me more and more
decisions.reason: The phrase is obscure. It seems to describe hangers-on who make jokes at others' expense in return for food; the ancient translations read it in different ways.

decisions.choice: gnashed their teeth: showed fury and hatred
decisions.reason: Grinding the teeth is a sign of rage against someone (37:12; Job 16:9).

records.source: אֲדֹנָי֮ כַּמָּ֪ה תִּ֫רְאֶ֥ה הָשִׁ֣יבָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשֹּׁאֵיהֶ֑ם מִ֝כְּפִירִ֗ים יְחִידָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: My Lord, how long will you look? Bring back my soul from their ravages, from young lions my only one.
pieces: Lord, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stand and watch? Bring me back from the ruin they cause; save my one and only life from the lions.

L.17: My Lord, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} look on? Bring back my soul from their ravages, my only [life] from [the] young lions.

R.17: Lord, how long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} just watch? Save me from their attacks. Save my life from these people who are like lions.

decisions.choice: my Lord: 'Adonai
decisions.reason: The title 'Adonai means "my Lord", master; it is not the divine name.

decisions.choice: my only one: my one life
decisions.reason: The word (yechidah) means "only one"; as in 22:21, it is his life, which he has only once.

decisions.choice: young lions: fierce enemies
decisions.reason: The enemies are pictured as lions tearing their prey (22:22).

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: In address, "Lord" carries the sense of "my Lord"; Literal keeps "my".

records.source: א֭וֹדְךָ בְּקָהָ֣ל רָ֑ב בְּעַ֖ם עָצ֣וּם אֲהַֽלְלֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: I will give you thanks in [the] great assembly; among a mighty people I will praise you.
pieces: I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} when the great congregation gathers; I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} among crowds of people.

L.18: I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} thanks in [the] great assembly; among a mighty people I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.18: I will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} when all the people come together to worship. In front of a huge crowd I will praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: the great assembly: the gathered worshipers
decisions.reason: Thanks for rescue were given in public, at the temple (22:26; 40:10).

decisions.choice: mighty: numerous
decisions.reason: The word ('atsum) means strong or numerous; here a large crowd.

records.source: אַֽל־יִשְׂמְחוּ־לִ֣י אֹיְבַ֣י שֶׁ֑קֶר שֹׂנְאַ֥י חִ֝נָּ֗ם יִקְרְצוּ־עָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: Let them not rejoice over me, my enemies [by] falsehood; those hating me without cause, let them wink [the] eye.
pieces: Do not let my lying enemies gloat over me; do not let those who hate me for nothing wink at each other.

L.19: Let not my lying enemies rejoice over me; [let not] those who hate me without cause wink [the] eye.

R.19: Do not let my enemies be happy about my troubles. They lie about me. They hate me for no reason. Do not let them wink at each other, sure that they have won.

decisions.choice: hate me without cause: John 15:25
decisions.reason: Jesus says that the word "they hated me without cause" is fulfilled in the hatred against him (John 15:25); the words are found here and in 69:5.

decisions.choice: falsehood: enemies with no just cause, who lie
decisions.reason: The word (sheqer) describes enemies whose hostility rests on lies.

decisions.choice: wink the eye: a sign of malice and triumph
decisions.reason: Winking signals a shared plot or gloating (Proverbs 6:13; 10:10).

decisions.choice: let them not ... let them wink: the "not" carries over
decisions.reason: The "not" of the first line governs the second as well.

decisions.choice: sure that they have won
decisions.reason: Readable says what the wink means (m3).

records.source: כִּ֤י לֹ֥א שָׁל֗וֹם יְדַ֫בֵּ֥רוּ וְעַ֥ל רִגְעֵי־אֶ֑רֶץ דִּבְרֵ֥י מִ֝רְמוֹת יַחֲשֹׁבֽוּן׃
records.gloss: For not peace they speak, and against [the] quiet of [the] land words of deceit they plan.
pieces: For they do not talk of peace; they dream up lies against people living quietly in the land.

L.20: For they do not speak peace, and against the quiet [ones] of [the] land they devise words of deceit.

R.20: They never say anything that brings peace. They make up lies about people who just want to live in peace.

decisions.choice: peace: words that seek good relations
decisions.reason: To speak peace (shalom) is to speak for well-being and harmony (85:9; Zechariah 9:10).

decisions.choice: the quiet of the land: peaceful, defenseless people
decisions.reason: The word (rega'im), found only here, describes people who live quietly and trust God rather than force.

records.source: וַיַּרְחִ֥יבוּ עָלַ֗י פִּ֫יהֶ֥ם אָ֭מְרוּ הֶאָ֣ח׀הֶאָ֑ח רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And they opened wide against me their mouth; they said, Aha, aha, our eye has seen.
pieces: They open their mouths wide at me and say, "Aha! Aha! We saw it with our own eyes!"

L.21: And they open wide their mouth against me; they say, "Aha, aha! Our eye has seen [it]!"

R.21: They laugh at me with their mouths wide open. They say, "Ha! Ha! Now we have seen it happen!"

decisions.choice: open wide the mouth: jeer and mock
decisions.reason: Opening the mouth wide is a gesture of scorn (22:14; Isaiah 57:4).

decisions.choice: our eye has seen: what we hoped to see
decisions.reason: They gloat over his downfall, or claim to have seen him do wrong; verse 22 answers that the LORD has seen.

records.source: רָאִ֣יתָה יְ֭הוָה אַֽל־תֶּחֱרַ֑שׁ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י אֲל־תִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: You have seen, YHWH; do not be silent; my Lord, do not be far from me.
pieces: You have seen it, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; do not keep silent. Lord, do not stay far away from me.

L.22: You have seen, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; do not be silent; my Lord, do not be far from me.

R.22: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have seen it all. Do not keep quiet. Lord, do not stay far away from me.

decisions.choice: You have seen: set against what they have seen
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 21. They boast of what they have seen; the LORD has seen everything.

decisions.choice: do not be silent: act and speak for me
decisions.reason: God's silence means not acting (28:1; 83:2).

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

records.source: הָעִ֣ירָה וְ֭הָקִיצָה לְמִשְׁפָּטִ֑י אֱלֹהַ֖י וַֽאדֹנָ֣י לְרִיבִֽי׃
records.gloss: Stir up and awake to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause.
pieces: Wake up! Rouse {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to do me justice; my God and my Lord, take up my case!

L.23: Stir up and awake to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause!

R.23: Wake up! Get up and defend me, my God and my Lord! Take my side in this case.

decisions.choice: wake up: act now
decisions.reason: The LORD does not sleep (121:4); the cry "wake up" asks him to act at once (44:24).

decisions.choice: my judgment, my cause: my case at law
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the psalmist asks God to take up his case as judge and defender.

records.source: שָׁפְטֵ֣נִי כְ֭צִדְקְךָ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֗י וְאַל־יִשְׂמְחוּ־לִֽי׃
records.gloss: Judge me according to your righteousness, YHWH my God, and let them not rejoice over me.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, give judgment for me as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness requires; let them not rejoice over me.

L.24: Judge me according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, and let them not rejoice over me.

R.24: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always do what is right, so show that I am in the right. Do not let my enemies laugh at me.

decisions.choice: judge me: decide my case in my favor
decisions.reason: To judge (shafat) someone here is to give a just verdict that sets them right (7:9; 26:1).

decisions.choice: your righteousness: your justice
decisions.reason: He appeals not to his own merit but to God's righteousness, his faithfulness to do what is right.

decisions.choice: my enemies
decisions.reason: Readable names who would rejoice.

records.source: אַל־יֹאמְר֣וּ בְ֭לִבָּם הֶאָ֣ח נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ אַל־יֹ֝אמְר֗וּ בִּֽלַּעֲנֽוּהוּ׃
records.gloss: Let them not say in their heart, Aha, our desire! Let them not say, We have swallowed him.
pieces: Do not let them say to themselves, "Aha! We got our wish!" Do not let them say, "We have gulped him down."

L.25: Let them not say in their heart, "Aha, our desire!" Let them not say, "We have swallowed him up."

R.25: Do not let them think, "Ha! We got what we wanted!" Do not let them say, "We have destroyed him."

decisions.choice: say in their heart: think
decisions.reason: To say in the heart is to think to oneself (10:6; 14:1).

decisions.choice: our desire: just what we wanted
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) here means appetite or desire (27:12).

decisions.choice: swallowed him: destroyed him completely
decisions.reason: As a beast swallows its prey (124:3; Lamentations 2:16).

records.source: יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּר֨וּ׀יַחְדָּו֮ שְׂמֵחֵ֪י רָעָ֫תִ֥י יִֽלְבְּשׁוּ־בֹ֥שֶׁת וּכְלִמָּ֑ה הַֽמַּגְדִּילִ֥ים עָלָֽי׃
records.gloss: Let them be ashamed and abashed together, [those] glad at my harm; let them be clothed with shame and disgrace, those making themselves great over me.
pieces: Let all who are glad at my trouble be shamed and confused together; let those who lift themselves up over me be dressed in shame and disgrace.

L.26: Let them be ashamed and confounded together who are glad at my harm; let them be clothed with shame and disgrace who make themselves great over me.

R.26: People who are happy when I suffer, let them all be ashamed and confused. People who act proud and look down on me, let shame and disgrace cover them like clothes.

decisions.choice: clothed with shame: covered with it
decisions.reason: Shame is pictured as clothing that wraps them completely (109:29; Job 8:22).

decisions.choice: Let them be ashamed: the prayer of verse 4 returns
decisions.reason: The psalm returns to the words of verse 4 as it draws to a close.

records.source: יָרֹ֣נּוּ וְיִשְׂמְחוּ֮ חֲפֵצֵ֪י צִ֫דְקִ֥י וְיֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה הֶ֝חָפֵ֗ץ שְׁל֣וֹם עַבְדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Let them shout for joy and be glad, those delighting in my righteousness, and let them say continually, Great be YHWH, who delights [in the] peace of his servant.
pieces: Let those who want to see me proved right shout with joy and be glad; let them say again and again, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great! He is pleased when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant has peace."

L.27: Let them shout for joy and be glad who delight in my righteousness, and let them say continually, "Great [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who delights in the peace of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant."

R.27: But let the people who want me to win my case shout and be happy. Let them always say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great! He is happy when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant has peace and does well."

decisions.choice: my righteousness: my being proved in the right
decisions.reason: The word (tsedeq) here is his right standing in the case: their wish is to see him cleared.

decisions.choice: peace: welfare, well-being
decisions.reason: Shalom here is the servant's safety and well-being, which the LORD delights to give.

decisions.choice: Great be the LORD: may he be seen to be great
decisions.reason: The verb is a wish: may the LORD be shown great, praised as great.

decisions.choice: see me proved right (B); want me to win my case (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m1).

records.source: וּ֭לְשׁוֹנִי תֶּהְגֶּ֣ה צִדְקֶ֑ךָ כָּל־הַ֝יּוֹם תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And my tongue will murmur your righteousness, all the day your praise.
pieces: Then all day long I will talk about how righteous {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are and sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

L.28: And my tongue will murmur {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, all the day {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

R.28: I will talk about {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness and praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all day long.

decisions.choice: murmur: speak, recite
decisions.reason: The verb (hagah) is the same as in 1:2, words spoken half aloud; here, telling God's righteousness.

decisions.choice: your righteousness: the answer to verse 24
decisions.reason: He asked to be judged by God's righteousness; now he will speak of it all day.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: The tongue stands for the speaker.
